h1: The 5 Best 1000-Watt Microwaves of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five 1000-watt microwaves from Toshiba, Sharp, GE and BLACK+DECKER, covering countertop and over-the-range picks by size.
summary: The Toshiba 1.2 cu ft countertop is our pick for most kitchens. The Toshiba with Smart Sensor adds sensor cooking, the Sharp SMC1162KS suits tighter counters, and the GE and BLACK+DECKER over-the-range models replace a stove hood.
intro: A 1000-watt rating is the point where a microwave stops feeling slow, but the wattage tells you nothing about whether the box will fit your kitchen. Over-the-range models and countertop models share the same wattage and need completely different spaces.

We reviewed five 1000W microwaves and ranked them on cooking capacity, mounting style and price bucket. Where a listing gives only capacity and wattage we stick to that, and you should check dimensions and features on the live page.

products.name: TOSHIBA Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A 1.2 cu ft, 1000W countertop with no drama.
products.description:
The TOSHIBA Countertop Microwave Oven pairs a 1.2 cu ft cavity with 1000W of power, in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks first because it combines a roomy cavity with a countertop footprint, without the install work of an over-the-range model. Against the Sharp below it offers more capacity, at the cost of more counter space.

Buy it if you want a standard family microwave. The caveat is the larger body, which needs real counter room.
products.idealFor: Families wanting a roomy countertop microwave.

products.name: TOSHIBA Countertop Microwave Oven with Smart Sensor
products.verdict: Same size and power as the top pick, plus a sensor.
products.description:
The TOSHIBA with Smart Sensor is a 1.2 cu ft, 1000W countertop microwave in the $100-200 bucket, and the name highlights a sensor feature.

It ranks second only because the base Toshiba gives you the same capacity and power, so the sensor is the single reason to pay attention to this one. Both sit in the same price bucket.

Buy it if you like the idea of sensor-assisted cooking. The caveat is that the listing facts do not detail how the sensor works.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want sensor features at standard size.
products.skipIf: You just want the plainer, proven model.

products.name: Sharp SMC1162KS 1.1 cu. ft. 1000W Stainless Steel Countertop
products.verdict: Slightly smaller cavity, stainless finish, same 1000W.
products.description:
The Sharp SMC1162KS is a 1.1 cu ft, 1000W countertop microwave in stainless steel, in the $100-200 bucket.

Third place comes down to the Toshibas offering 0.1 cu ft more room. Its advantage is a slightly smaller body and a stainless look that suits modern kitchens.

Buy it if you want a tidy stainless unit. The caveat is that the cavity is a little smaller for large dishes.
products.idealFor: Kitchens with a stainless theme and limited counter room.

products.name: GE 30" Over-the-Range Microwave
products.verdict: Frees the counter and doubles as a range hood.
products.description:
The GE 30" Over-the-Range Microwave lists a 1.6 cu ft cavity beside a 300 CFM hood vent and LED lighting, with 1000 watts of power, in the $200-500 bucket.

Fourth place reflects the fact that it needs installation above a range and costs more than the countertop picks. In return it clears counter space and adds ventilation the others lack.

Buy it if you are replacing a hood. The caveat is that it only suits a 30 inch range opening.
products.idealFor: Kitchens replacing a range hood with a microwave.
products.skipIf: You have no wall space above the range.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Over the Range Microwave Oven
products.verdict: The largest cavity here, but it needs installing.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER Over the Range microwave offers a 1.7 cu ft cavity and 1000W, in the $200-500 bucket.

Last place goes here since the GE adds a listed 300 CFM vent and LED lighting, while this listing gives only capacity and power. It does win on interior size.

Buy it if you want the most space above the stove. The caveat is that we cannot confirm vent or lighting details from the facts.
products.idealFor: Big households replacing a range hood.

whatMatters.detail: Capacity is the interior volume in cubic feet. It matters because a 1.1 cu ft cavity handles fewer large plates than 1.6 or 1.7. Check the cu ft figure in the title and think about your biggest dish.

Countertop models plug in anywhere, while over-the-range units mount above the stove and often act as a hood. It matters because the wrong choice means no space or a failed install. Measure your counter or range width before buying.
Wattage is cooking power. At 1000W food heats faster than on weaker models. Look for the number in the title, not just a marketing phrase like 'powerful'.
Over-the-range models can include a hood fan, measured in CFM. It matters because it handles cooktop steam. Check for a listed CFM figure, like the 300 CFM on the GE.
The five picks span $100-200 to $200-500. It matters because over-the-range convenience costs more. Decide whether you need the install before paying for it.

faq.a: For most home cooking and reheating, yes. All five picks here list 1000W.

faq.q: What is the biggest buying mistake?
faq.a: Assuming wattage tells you about size. Measure your counter or range opening before ordering.

faq.q: Is the Smart Sensor Toshiba worth it?
faq.a: Only if you want sensor-assisted cooking. The base Toshiba matches it on capacity and power.
Yes, they mount above the range. Plan for wall space and a compatible opening.
Wipe the interior after spills and keep vents clear. Follow the manual for filters on hood models.

faq.q: Why is the LG not here?
faq.a: Its listing does not state 1000W, so it does not match the title.

finalTake: The TOSHIBA Countertop Microwave Oven is the safest buy for most kitchens. The Sharp suits tighter counters, and the GE is the pick for a range hood swap. Match your space first and wattage second.
